decisionBasis: owner decision D1 2026-11-14: sibling-branch pairs in this repository
owner decision D3 2026-11-14: GO rule on System-2-unknown DP-1 pairs

method.where: throwaway mirror clone outside the repository; nothing written to the repository, the S1.5b store or the shadow store; no record kept
method.tips: unique commits of refs/heads, refs/remotes and refs/archive not merged into origin/develop
method.authorship: a tip is kept only if every commit between its develop fork point and the tip is owner-authored (matched in memory, never stored)
method.pairs: every unordered pair of kept tips whose own change set is at most 64 paths; base = git merge-base of the pair; pairs whose base equals one side are not diverged
method.pathBound: each side at most 64 changed paths against the pair base (git_replay.MAX_PATHS); a cheap superset bound (more than 256 develop paths between the two fork points) skips cross-fork pairs that cannot meet it
method.oracle: git merge-tree --write-tree --no-messages: exit 0 merge-clean, exit 1 merge-conflict
method.system2: the agent_braid analysis rule applied to git name-status --no-renames against the pair base: a path that both sides add or modify (A or M) is a shared write resource, so conflicting; otherwise any status other than A or M (a deletion or type change, which git_adapter records as a per-operation git-unsupported resource with kind unknown and partial coverage, never shared) is unknown; otherwise independent-candidate. No dependencies and no uncertain paths, as in the T106 request. A review-time rerun with this exact sharing rule (deleted paths never shared) gave identical counts.

d3Need.rule: Wilson 95% upper bound of false independence at most 2% and coverage at least 30% on System-2-unknown DP-1 pairs, early stop allowed
d3Need.plusSplits: train and calibration splits on top of the evaluation pairs

projection.upperBoundIfEveryCrossForkPairBeyondTheB: about 70 at the observed share (53537 x 0.0013); most of those exceed 64 paths, so the true figure is lower
projection.shortfallFactorAgainstEvalNeedAlone: about 157x now; at least 9x even under the upper bound
projection.accumulationPath: none credible: System 2 says unknown on a git pair only when the two change sets are disjoint and one side deletes or changes the type of a file, which owner branches rarely do; the live shadow pool (plan R-D) is about 142 pairs per 30-day window, of which about 27 percent are DP-1 across all kinds, and the population is not widened after labels are seen

limits: Counts only: no commit id, path, author, message or ref name is recorded.

The System 2 class is the analysis rule applied to name-status output, not a run of analyze_git_with_provenance on every pair; it matches that rule for commit sources without dependencies or uncertain paths.
Sibling pairs reuse tips: 3015 labelled pairs come from 361 tips and 205 merge bases, so the effective sample is far smaller than the pair count; this strengthens the INFEASIBLE verdict.
merge-tree labels textual cleanliness, not semantic independence.
No scientific claim; nothing here measures System One accuracy or utility.
consequence: T104 stays stopped for the System-2-unknown population: the sibling source cannot reach the D3 need. The sibling origin is not added to the T106 tool and no real dry run is made.
